chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, or someone else, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said:

There was a man in Makkah, a client of the Banu Umayya, called Ibn Abi 'Awanah, who had obstinacy (towards the Ahl al-Bayt). And whenever Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) or one of the elders of the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon them) entered Makkah, he would abuse him.
And indeed, he came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while he was in the Tawaf, and he said, 'O Abu Abdillah! What do you say regarding touching the Stone?'
He (peace be upon him) said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) touched it.' He said to him, 'I do not see you touching it.'
He (peace be upon him) said, 'I dislike that I should hurt the weak ones or be hurt (due to congestion).'
He said, 'So you have claimed that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) touched it.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes.'
'But it was so that whenever the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was seen, they recognized his right for him, and as for me, they do not recognize my right for me.'

key_terms.أَشْيَاخُ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: Elders of the Family of Muhammad
key_terms.اسْتِلَامُ الْحَجَر: Touching the Stone (specifically the Black Stone)

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) not touch the Black Stone directly during Tawaf?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the principle of *Taqiyya* (prudent dissimulation) through Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) strategic avoidance of the Black Stone, not due to lack of reverence, but to prevent physical harm from the crowd who did not recognize his status. It highlights the distinction between the Prophet’s inherent authority, which commanded immediate respect, and the Imam’s need to navigate social dynamics while maintaining ritual correctness. This incident serves as a key scholarly reference for understanding how the Imams balanced public ritual observance with private spiritual intent and physical safety.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, or someone else from Mhammad Bin Usman who said,

‘There was a man in Makkah who was a slave of the Clan of Umayya called Ibn Abu Awana who had obstinacy for him, and whenever Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> or any one from the Sheykhs<sup>as</sup> of the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> entered Makkah, he would abuse them<sup>as</sup>.
And he came to Abu Abdullahasws while heasws was in the Tawaaf, and he said, ‘O Abu Abdullahasws! What are youasws saying regarding touching the (Black) Stone?’
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> touched it’. So he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I did not see you<sup>asws</sup> touching it’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> disliked that I<sup>asws</sup> should hurt the weak ones or be hurt (due to congestion)’.
So he said, ‘But you<sup>asws</sup> have claimed that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> touched it’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, but it was so that whenever Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was seen, they recognised his<sup>saww</sup> right for him<sup>saww</sup> (and made way for him<sup>saww</sup>), and as for me<sup>asws</sup>, they are not recognising my<sup>asws</sup> right for me<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 17. Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali or others from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman who has said the following:

“In Makkah there was a man of the friends of Banu ‘Umayyah called ibn abu ‘Awanah who had hostility. Whenever abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, or any shaykh from the family of Muhammad, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, entered Makkah, he mocked.
He came to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, during his performing Tawaf and said, ‘O abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, what do you say about touching the Black Stone?’
He (the Imam) said, ‘The Messenger of Allah touched it.’ He said, ‘But I do not see you touching it.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘I do not like to disturb weak people or be disturbed.’
He then said, ‘But you believe that the Messenger of Allah would touch it.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes,
but when people would see the Messenger of Allah they recognize his rights and in my case they do not recognize it.’”
